definitions.explanation: A wide, well-traveled street that is the primary thoroughfare in an area, as opposed to back streets or side streets.

examples.japanese: {表通|おもてどお}りに{面|めん}した{店|みせ}。
examples.english: A shop facing the main street.

examples.japanese: {表通|おもてどお}りは{人通|ひとどお}りが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There is a lot of foot traffic on the main street.

examples.japanese: {表通|おもてどお}りから{一本|いっぽん}{入|はい}った{路地|ろじ}に{隠|かく}れた{名店|めいてん}がある。
examples.english: There's a hidden gem of a restaurant in an alley one block off the main street.

notes:
USAGE:
Contrasts with {裏通|うらどお}り (back street, side street). Properties facing the {表通|おもてどお}り tend to have higher rent and more visibility.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表通|おもてどお}りに{面|めん}する (to face the main street)
- {表通|おもてどお}り{沿|ぞ}い (along the main street)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {裏通|うらどお}り: back street — a quieter, narrower side street behind the main road
- {大通|おおどお}り: wide avenue — a major boulevard, often wider than {表通|おもてどお}り
